top_story_title: SonicWall SMA 1000 remote-access appliances under active attack via maximum-severity SSRF
top_story_summary: Attackers are exploiting a critical server-side request forgery vulnerability in SonicWall SMA 1000 series appliances, the remote-access gateways that front internal applications for remote and third-party users. The flaw is rated maximum severity and exploitation is reported as ongoing, which puts every internet-facing SMA 1000 in scope regardless of whether a given organisation has seen alerts yet.
top_actions: Inventory every SonicWall SMA 1000 appliance with its exact model and running firmware build, and flag which ones are reachable from the internet.
Check the SonicWall advisory for the fixed release that applies to your SMA 1000 firmware line, and schedule the upgrade as an emergency change - this is under active exploitation.
Remove the appliance management interface (HTTPS/SSH/API) from internet exposure now; restrict administration to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network.
Restrict inbound access to the portal to required source geographies/ASNs as an interim control while the upgrade is staged.
After upgrading, terminate all active sessions and revoke session tokens, then rotate local admin credentials, certificates and any secrets stored on the appliance.
executive_summary: SonicWall SMA 1000 remote-access appliances are being actively exploited through a maximum-severity SSRF flaw; treat internet-facing units as an emergency change.
No CVE ID or fixed build is stated in the available reporting - get the fixed-release table from the SonicWall advisory for your model before scheduling the upgrade.
SSRF on a VPN gateway is an internal-network reach problem, not just an appliance problem: pair the upgrade with session revocation and secret rotation.
Quiet collection window otherwise - one qualifying network-device item in the last 24 hours, and no AI-related network-device news.
key_actions: **SonicWall** — Identify all SMA 1000 appliances from asset inventory with model and running firmware build; mark which are internet-reachable.
**SonicWall** — Check the vendor advisory for the fixed release covering your firmware line, then patch to that build and run the vendor Integrity Checker Tool if one is offered for this platform.

headlines.title: Maximum-Severity SSRF Flaw in SonicWall SMA Devices Under Attack
headlines.summary: A maximum-severity SSRF vulnerability in SonicWall SMA 1000 remote-access appliances is being exploited in active attacks.
